title: Testing, Debugging, and Deployment
summary: Prove your code works, find out why it doesn't, and ship it safely to production.

lessons.title: Test Data That Never Lies
lessons.objective: Given a scenario, determine how to test Apex classes and triggers, including the use of mocks and stubs (HttpCalloutMock, Stub API, Test.startTest/stopTest, test data).

cards.title: In plain words
cards.body: A test needs data to work on. Real records change from org to org, so tests shouldn't lean on them. Salesforce gives every test an **empty database**, and you build exactly what it needs. Same data every run means the same result every run.

cards.title: Think of it like…
cards.body: A cooking show. The chef doesn't raid your fridge. Every ingredient is measured out on the counter before the cameras roll. Where it stops: a few kitchen basics are always there, like `User`, `Profile`, `RecordType` and `Organization`.

cards.title: Empty org by default
cards.body: Since API **24.0**, tests **can't see org data**. Only setup-type objects show up: `User`, `Profile`, `RecordType`, `Organization`. Business records and custom setting records stay hidden. `@isTest(SeeAllData=true)` opens everything, and you almost never want it.

cards.title: Test data factory
cards.body: A **test data factory** (one shared class that builds records) makes Accounts for any test. A new required field? Fix it here once.

cards.title: @TestSetup
cards.body: **@TestSetup** runs once per class. Each test method gets a fresh copy, and its changes roll back before the next. Statics set there don't carry over, so query the records.

cards.title: Data from a CSV
cards.body: `Test.loadData` reads a CSV **static resource** (a file stored in Salesforce) and inserts its rows. Handy when admins own the sample data.

cards.title: SOSL in tests
cards.body: **SOSL** (Salesforce's text search) returns **nothing** in a test, even for records the test inserted. Call `Test.setFixedSearchResults(ids)` to tell it which Ids to return.
**SeeAllData=true** ties tests to whatever is in the org, so they break in the next sandbox. And **@TestSetup is not supported** in a class marked `@isTest(SeeAllData=true)`.

cards.title: Remember it
cards.body: "**Bring your own lunch.**" Tests eat only the data they pack: a factory, `@TestSetup` or `Test.loadData`. And SOSL is shy in tests, so give it a script.

lessons.title: startTest, stopTest, Async Magic
lessons.objective: Given a scenario, determine how to test Apex classes and triggers, including the use of mocks and stubs (HttpCalloutMock, Stub API, Test.startTest/stopTest, test data).

cards.title: In plain words
cards.body: Tests have two problems. Setup code eats into **governor limits** (hard caps per transaction, like 100 SOQL queries). And **async code** (code that runs later, in the background) won't finish before your test checks it. `Test.startTest()` and `Test.stopTest()` fix both.

cards.title: Think of it like…
cards.body: A race with a stopwatch. `startTest()` resets the clock, so the runner gets fresh limits. `stopTest()` is the finish line: every job still running must cross it right then. Where it stops: you get only **one** race per test method.

cards.title: What startTest/stopTest do
items: Code between them gets a **fresh set of governor limits**
Async work queued between them (future, queueable, batch, scheduled) **runs synchronously at stopTest()**
After stopTest(), the limits from before startTest() come back
Only **one** startTest/stopTest pair per test method

cards.title: Testing Batch Apex
cards.body: The batch runs at `stopTest()`, so assert **after** it. A test can run only **one `execute()` chunk**, so keep records within the scope size (default 200).

cards.title: Scheduled Apex
cards.body: Call `System.schedule` between start and stop. The job's `execute()` runs at **stopTest()**, whatever the cron says. To check the schedule itself, query **CronTrigger** (the record that holds the cron expression and next fire time).

cards.title: Platform events
cards.body: Published events wait on a **test event bus** until `stopTest()` or `Test.getEventBus().deliver()`. Each `deliver()` sends only what is waiting right now.

cards.title: Parallel tests have rules
cards.body: `@IsTest(IsParallel=true)` lets tests run side by side for speed. But those tests **can't call** `System.schedule()`, `System.enqueueJob()` or `Test.getStandardPricebookId()`.
**Chaining a queueable** (enqueueing a job from inside a queueable) can throw an error in a test. The docs suggest guarding the chain call with `Test.isRunningTest()` and testing one link.

cards.title: Remember it
cards.body: "**Stop means Go.**" Async code doesn't run until you hit `stopTest()`. Asserts before it see the world before the job ran.

lessons.title: Run As, Assert, Don't Cheat
lessons.objective: Given a scenario, determine how to test Apex classes and triggers, including the use of mocks and stubs (HttpCalloutMock, Stub API, Test.startTest/stopTest, test data).

cards.title: In plain words
cards.body: Some code acts differently for different users. **System.runAs** lets a test pretend to be another user for a block of code. You also need **asserts** (checks that fail the test when a result is wrong). A test without asserts proves nothing.

cards.title: Think of it like…
cards.body: Borrowing a friend's library card. You can only open the shelves their card unlocks: that's record sharing. Nobody checks which pages you may read: that's field and object permissions. Your code must check those itself.

cards.title: System.runAs(user)
cards.body: `System.runAs` enforces **record sharing** only. It does **not** enforce **object or field permissions** for code in system mode (code that ignores the user's permissions). To test permissions, the code must check them: `WITH USER_MODE`, `AccessLevel.USER_MODE` or `stripInaccessible`.

cards.title: More runAs facts
items: Works only in test methods
Inserts a User you built but didn't insert yet
Ignores user license limits
**Each call counts** against the 150 DML statement limit

cards.title: Mixed DML fix
cards.body: **Setup objects** (like `User`, `Group`, `PermissionSetAssignment`) can't be saved in the same transaction as normal records. That throws **MIXED_DML_OPERATION**. Wrap the setup DML in `System.runAs()`, or move it to an **@future** method. A User with no `UserRoleId` is exempt.

cards.title: Assert class + expected exceptions
cards.body: **Assert.fail** fails the test when no exception is thrown. A failed assert **can't be caught**, even by `catch (Exception e)`. Others: `areEqual(expected, actual)`, `isNull`, `isInstanceOfType`.
`if (Test.isRunningTest())` branches make tests run **different code than production**. Coverage looks fine while real bugs hide. Use mocks and dependency injection instead.

cards.title: Remember it
cards.body: runAs = "**Records, not Rights.**" It changes whose records you can see, not what you're allowed to do.

lessons.title: Fake the Internet: Callout Mocks
lessons.objective: Given a scenario, determine how to test Apex classes and triggers, including the use of mocks and stubs (HttpCalloutMock, Stub API, Test.startTest/stopTest, test data).

cards.title: In plain words
cards.body: A **callout** is your code calling another system over the internet. Tests **can't make real callouts**, because the outside world is slow and unpredictable. So you give the test a **mock**: a fake that returns a ready-made answer. Register it with `Test.setMock()`, or the test fails.

cards.title: Think of it like…
cards.body: A fire drill. Nobody lights a real fire. A bell rings and everyone acts as if. The mock is the bell: your code runs its real steps, but the fire is fake. Where it stops: you must ring the bell (`Test.setMock`) before the code needs it.

cards.title: HttpCalloutMock
cards.body: One method: `respond(HttpRequest)` returns a fake **HttpResponse**. Read `req.getEndpoint()` to answer different URLs.

cards.title: Many endpoints, static resources
cards.body: One endpoint? **StaticResourceCalloutMock** (the same body for every call). Several? **MultiStaticResourceCalloutMock** maps each URL to its own static resource.

cards.title: SOAP (WSDL2Apex)
cards.body: **WSDL2Apex** (a tool that turns a WSDL file into Apex) makes SOAP classes. Mock them with **WebServiceMock**: `doInvoke` returns nothing and puts the reply in the map under **response_x**.

"**You have uncommitted work pending**" means DML came before a callout. Do the test **DML before `Test.startTest()`**, then make the callout **inside** startTest/stopTest. For async callouts, register the mock **before `stopTest()`**.

cards.title: Remember it
cards.body: **H**TTP gets **H**ttpCalloutMock and `respond`. **S**OAP gets WebServiceMock, `doInvoke` and **response_x**. Either way: **set the mock first**.

lessons.title: Stub API: Mock Your Own Classes
lessons.objective: Given a scenario, determine how to test Apex classes and triggers, including the use of mocks and stubs (HttpCalloutMock, Stub API, Test.startTest/stopTest, test data).

cards.title: In plain words
cards.body: You want to test class A, but A uses class B. B is slow, makes callouts or needs lots of setup. The **Stub API** builds a fake B while the test runs. A talks to the fake, so you test A on its own.

cards.title: Think of it like…
cards.body: A stunt double in a movie. The director swaps the star for a double, and the scene still works. Where it stops: the script needs a spot for the swap. If A builds its own B with `new`, there's no way in.

cards.title: StubProvider
cards.body: Every call on the stub lands in **handleMethodCall**. You pick the return value by method name, return type or arguments. Unmatched calls can return `null`.

cards.title: Create and inject
cards.body: `Test.createStub(Type, StubProvider)` returns an Object, so **cast it**. Then **inject** it (pass it in) to the class under test.

cards.title: Can't be stubbed
items: **Static** methods (incl. future)
**Private** methods
Properties (getters/setters)
Triggers, inner classes, system types
Batchable classes, classes with only private constructors
Classes outside the namespace of the `createStub()` call

cards.title: No built-in verify
cards.body: The Stub API has **no `verify()`** and no `when()`. To prove a call happened, record `stubbedMethodName` and `listOfArgs` inside `handleMethodCall`. Then assert on what you recorded.

The Stub API **doesn't intercept `new`**. If `InvoiceBuilder` calls `new TaxService()` itself, the stub never gets used. Add a **seam**: a constructor or setter that accepts the dependency. Making the method static won't help.

cards.title: Remember it
cards.body: "**No seam, no swap.**" The class must accept its helper from outside, or there's nothing to replace.

lessons.title: Testing LWC (Jest) and VF Controllers
lessons.objective: Given a scenario, identify how to test and debug Lightning web components, Aura components, Visualforce, and JavaScript (including Jest unit tests for LWC).

cards.title: In plain words
cards.body: Lightning web components (**LWC**, Salesforce's JavaScript UI pieces) get their own tests. They use **Jest**, a JavaScript test tool. Jest checks what a component shows and does, right on your computer. Visualforce pages are tested with Apex instead.

cards.title: Think of it like…
cards.body: A flight simulator. Pilots practice on the ground while fake weather is fed in. Jest is the simulator: no org, no browser, and you feed in fake data. Where it stops: simulator hours **don't count** toward Apex code coverage.

cards.title: Jest = local unit tests
cards.body: Jest runs in **Node.js** via **@salesforce/sfdx-lwc-jest**. Tests live in a **__tests__** folder, named `*.test.js`. **Append the element to the DOM** first: a component gets wire data only once connected. Reach inner elements through `element.shadowRoot`.

cards.title: Mock a wire adapter
cards.body: Wire adapters become **test adapters**: `.emit(data)` pushes data, `.error()` pushes an error, `getLastConfig()` shows what the component asked for. Wired Apex uses `createApexTestWireAdapter`.

cards.title: Mock imperative Apex
cards.body: Mocks an Apex method that is called imperatively. **virtual: true** is needed because the Apex module isn't on disk. Then set results with `mockResolvedValue` or `mockRejectedValue`.
DOM updates are **async**. After you set a property or emit data, **`await Promise.resolve()`** (or a flushPromises helper) before you assert.

cards.title: Debugging LWC in the browser
items: **Debug Mode** (per user, in Setup): JavaScript is not minified
**Pause on exceptions** (DevTools Sources): stops at the line that throws
**Enable custom formatters**: shows real values inside LWC proxies
Sandbox only: clear **secure and persistent browser caching** to load new code
`sfdx-lwc-jest --debug` plus **chrome://inspect**: breakpoints in Jest tests

cards.title: Visualforce extension test
cards.body: Sets the page and its URL params, then wraps the record in a **StandardController**. Call action methods, then check `ApexPages.hasMessages()` or `ApexPages.getMessages()`.

cards.title: Remember it
cards.body: The Jest recipe: "**Append, emit, await, assert.**" Put the element on the page, push the data, wait one tick, then check.

lessons.title: Debug Like a Detective
lessons.objective: Given a scenario, determine why Apex code is not behaving as expected and how to debug it (debug logs, checkpoints, Apex Replay Debugger).

cards.title: In plain words
cards.body: When code misbehaves, you need to see what it did. A **debug log** (a record of what happened in a transaction) shows you. **Trace flags** decide whose logs get written and how much detail they hold. Debuggers then let you step through it.

cards.title: Think of it like…
cards.body: A security camera. The **trace flag** says which door to watch and for how long. The **debug level** is the zoom. The **log** is the footage you review later. Where it stops: a class trace flag only changes the zoom; it doesn't switch the camera on.

cards.title: Log levels (quiet to loud)
items: NONE
ERROR
WARN
INFO
DEBUG
FINE
FINER
FINEST

cards.title: Trace flags
cards.body: A **trace flag** = who to log + a **debug level** + a time window (max **24 hours**). Set it on a **user**, an **Apex class/trigger** or the Automated Process. **Class/trigger flags override** levels for that code, so you can mute a chatty class. They don't start logging on their own.

cards.title: Apex Replay Debugger
cards.body: Free, in **VS Code**. Capture a log with Apex Code at **FINEST**, then replay it: **breakpoints**, variables, call stack. **Checkpoints** add heap dumps. It works on any org, even production, because it only reads logs.

cards.title: Developer Console
cards.body: **Checkpoints** (up to **5**) take a heap snapshot at a line, with no code changes. The **Query Editor** runs SOQL. **Execution Overview** and the Timeline show slow spots.

cards.title: Limits class
cards.code:
System.debug(Limits.getQueries() + ' of ' + Limits.getLimitQueries() + ' SOQL used');
System.debug('CPU ms: ' + Limits.getCpuTime());
cards.body: `getX()` is what you've used so far; `getLimitX()` is the max. Check before you hit it: a **LimitException** can't be caught.
Unhandled exception emails go to the **last developer who modified** the class or trigger. Anyone added in Setup > **Apex Exception Email** gets them too.

cards.title: Remember it
cards.body: "**Every Wise Investigator Digs For Finer Facts**" = Error, Warn, Info, Debug, Fine, Finer, Finest. A message shows only if **Apex Code** is at its level or louder.

lessons.title: Orgs, CLI, Packages, Change Sets
lessons.objective: Given a scenario, formulate the deployment process, supporting tools, and mechanisms for source-driven development (Salesforce CLI, scratch orgs, packages, metadata/destructive changes).

cards.title: In plain words
cards.body: Code is built in one org and shipped to another. You need safe places to build and test, and a way to move changes. **Sandboxes** and **scratch orgs** are the workshops. **Change sets**, the **CLI** and **packages** are the delivery trucks.

cards.title: Think of it like…
cards.body: Building a house. A **sandbox** is a practice copy of the real house. A **scratch org** is a pop-up tent built from blueprints (your Git repo), then thrown away. A **package** is a flat-pack kit you can ship and upgrade. Where it stops: only Partial Copy and Full sandboxes copy real data.

cards.title: Sandbox cheat sheet
items: **Developer**: metadata only, no prod data (200 MB), refresh daily
**Developer Pro**: metadata only, more storage (1 GB), refresh daily
**Partial Copy**: metadata + sample data via **sandbox template**, refresh every **5 days**
**Full**: complete copy, refresh every **29 days** - perf/UAT/staging

cards.title: Scratch org loop (sf CLI)
cards.code:
sf org create scratch --definition-file config/project-scratch-def.json \
  --alias feature1 --duration-days 7 --target-dev-hub DevHub
sf project deploy start --target-org feature1
sf project retrieve start --target-org feature1
cards.body: Creates a scratch org and moves source in and out. Scratch orgs are throwaway (1-30 days), built from source, with **source tracking** (it notes what changed locally and in the org). They come from a **Dev Hub**.

cards.title: Packages
cards.body: **Unlocked packages** (2GP) are versioned, upgradeable bundles of your metadata, built from source with a Dev Hub. To **promote** a version to released, it needs **75% Apex code coverage**. So create it with `--code-coverage`, never with `--skip-validation`.

**Change sets** only work between orgs tied to the **same production org**. They need a **deployment connection** and **can't delete** components. To delete, deploy **destructiveChanges.xml** with the Metadata API or CLI.

cards.title: Deleting metadata
cards.body: Deletes the `LegacyHelper` class. Pair a destructive manifest with a `package.xml`. **Post** (`--post-destructive-changes`) deletes after the rest deploys; **pre** deletes first.

cards.title: DevOps Center
cards.body: **DevOps Center** is a click-based pipeline backed by Git. Each **work item**'s changes are committed to source control and promoted through **pipeline stages**. It's the modern replacement for change sets.

cards.title: Remember it
cards.body: Sandbox refresh days: "**1, 1, 5, 29**" = Developer, Developer Pro, Partial Copy, Full. And change sets **add, never subtract**.

lessons.title: Test Levels, Coverage, Quick Deploy
lessons.objective: Given a scenario, formulate the deployment process, supporting tools, and mechanisms for source-driven development (Salesforce CLI, scratch orgs, packages, metadata/destructive changes).

cards.title: In plain words
cards.body: Before Apex reaches production, Salesforce runs tests to prove it works. **Code coverage** is the share of your code lines that tests actually ran. A **test level** picks which tests run. Break these rules and the deploy fails.

cards.title: Think of it like…
cards.body: Airport security. Production is the plane. Your code can't board without passing the scanner (tests) and having 75% of its ticket stamped (coverage). **Quick deploy** is a pass from a check you already cleared, good for 10 days.

cards.title: Production deploy rules
items: **75%** org-wide Apex coverage
Every **trigger** has some coverage
All tests that run must **pass**
Test classes and System.debug lines don't count toward coverage

cards.title: Test levels
items: **NoTestRun** - default for non-production (not allowed in prod for Apex)
**RunSpecifiedTests** - only listed tests; **each** class/trigger deployed needs **75%** from them
**RunLocalTests** - all except tests from installed managed and unlocked packages; prod default when deploying Apex
**RunAllTestsInOrg** - everything, including managed packages

cards.title: Validate now, deploy later
cards.code:
sf project deploy validate --source-dir force-app \
  --test-level RunLocalTests --target-org prod
sf project deploy quick --job-id 0AfXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX --target-org prod
cards.body: Validates against production, then deploys that job later without re-running tests. **Quick deploy** works within **10 days** of a passing validation. `--use-most-recent` only looks back 3 days.

cards.title: Checking a sandbox
cards.body: `sf project deploy validate` is for **production**. To check a sandbox without changing it, run `sf project deploy start --dry-run` with a `--test-level`. `deploy preview` only lists changes and runs no tests.
RunSpecifiedTests checks coverage **per component**, not org-wide. 85% org-wide doesn't save a class sitting at 60%.

cards.title: Flows too
cards.body: If "**Deploy processes and flows as active**" is on, production also checks flows. Tests must cover **75%** of active autolaunched flows and processes.

cards.title: Remember it
cards.body: "**75 everywhere**": 75% org-wide, 75% per class with RunSpecifiedTests, 75% to promote a package, 75% of active flows. And every trigger needs **some** coverage.

flashcards.front: Can an Apex test see the records already in the org?
flashcards.back: No. Since API 24.0, tests start with an empty database. Setup-type objects like User, Profile, RecordType and Organization still show. Use SeeAllData=true only when you truly must.

flashcards.front: How often does an @TestSetup method run?
flashcards.back: Once per test class. Each test method gets a fresh copy of its records, and one method's changes roll back before the next.

flashcards.front: Can you use @TestSetup in a class with SeeAllData=true?
flashcards.back: No. Test setup methods aren't supported in a class annotated @isTest(SeeAllData=true).

flashcards.front: What does Test.loadData do?
flashcards.back: It inserts the rows of a CSV static resource and returns them: Test.loadData(Account.sObjectType, 'ResourceName') returns a List<sObject>.

flashcards.front: Why does SOSL find nothing in a test?
flashcards.back: SOSL always returns empty results in tests. Call Test.setFixedSearchResults(List<Id>) to choose what it returns.

flashcards.front: What are the two jobs of Test.startTest() and stopTest()?
flashcards.back: 1) The code between them gets fresh governor limits. 2) Async work queued between them runs synchronously when stopTest() is called.

flashcards.front: How many startTest/stopTest pairs can one test method have?
flashcards.back: Just one pair per test method.

flashcards.front: What's the key limit when testing Batch Apex?
flashcards.back: Only one execute() chunk can run in a test. Insert no more records than the batch scope, and assert after Test.stopTest().

flashcards.front: How do you deliver platform events in a test?
flashcards.back: Call Test.stopTest() or Test.getEventBus().deliver(). Until then, events wait on the test event bus. Test.getEventBus().fail() fakes a failed publish.

flashcards.front: How does scheduled Apex run in a test?
flashcards.back: Call System.schedule between start and stop. The job runs at stopTest(), whatever the cron says. Query CronTrigger to check the schedule.

flashcards.front: What does System.runAs enforce?
flashcards.back: Only the user's record sharing. It doesn't enforce object or field permissions for code running in system mode.

flashcards.front: How do you fix MIXED_DML_OPERATION in a test?
flashcards.back: Keep setup-object DML (User, Group, PermissionSetAssignment) apart: wrap it in System.runAs(), or do it in an @future method.

flashcards.front: Which comes first in Assert.areEqual: expected or actual?
flashcards.back: Expected first: Assert.areEqual(expected, actual, optionalMessage). Others: isTrue, isFalse, isNull, isNotNull, isInstanceOfType, fail.

flashcards.front: Why avoid if (Test.isRunningTest()) branches?
flashcards.back: Tests then run different code than production, so the real path goes untested. Use mocks or dependency injection instead.

flashcards.front: What method does HttpCalloutMock need, and how do you register it?
flashcards.back: HttpResponse respond(HttpRequest req). Register it with Test.setMock(HttpCalloutMock.class, new MyMock()).

flashcards.front: What method does WebServiceMock need?
flashcards.back: doInvoke(stub, request, response map, endpoint, soapAction, requestName, responseNS, responseName, responseType). It returns nothing: put the result in the response map under 'response_x'.

flashcards.front: When do you use StaticResourceCalloutMock or MultiStaticResourceCalloutMock?
flashcards.back: Static: one canned response from one static resource, for every call. Multi: each endpoint gets its own static resource.

flashcards.front: How do you fix "You have uncommitted work pending" in a test?
flashcards.back: Do the DML before Test.startTest(). Make the mocked callout between startTest() and stopTest().

flashcards.front: How do you create a stub with the Stub API?
flashcards.back: (MyType) Test.createStub(MyType.class, new MyStubProvider()). The provider implements System.StubProvider and its handleMethodCall method.

flashcards.front: What can't the Stub API mock?
flashcards.back: Static and private methods, properties, classes with only private constructors, triggers, inner classes, system types and Batchable classes.

flashcards.front: Where do LWC Jest tests run?
flashcards.back: On your own computer, in Node.js, using @salesforce/sfdx-lwc-jest. Files go in __tests__ and are named *.test.js. No org needed.

flashcards.front: How do you push mock data through a wire adapter in Jest?
flashcards.back: Call emit on the adapter, like getRecord.emit(mock), or error() for an error. Then await Promise.resolve() before you assert.

flashcards.front: Why does jest.mock need { virtual: true } for Apex imports?
flashcards.back: @salesforce/apex/... modules don't exist on disk. virtual: true lets Jest mock a module it can't find.

flashcards.front: What are the debug log levels, from quietest to loudest?
flashcards.back: NONE, ERROR, WARN, INFO, DEBUG, FINE, FINER, FINEST.

flashcards.front: How long can a trace flag last?
flashcards.back: At most 24 hours.

flashcards.front: What is a class-level trace flag for?
flashcards.back: It overrides log levels for one class or trigger. Example: set Apex Code to ERROR to mute a noisy utility class. It doesn't start logging by itself.

flashcards.front: What does the Apex Replay Debugger need?
flashcards.back: A debug log captured with Apex Code at FINEST, replayed in VS Code. You get breakpoints, variables and checkpoints (heap dumps).

flashcards.front: How many Developer Console checkpoints can you set, and what do they do?
flashcards.back: Up to 5. Each captures the heap and variable values at a line, without changing code.

flashcards.front: How often can each sandbox type be refreshed?
flashcards.back: Developer and Developer Pro: every 1 day. Partial Copy: every 5 days. Full: every 29 days.

flashcards.front: How do you delete metadata from production?
flashcards.back: Deploy a destructiveChanges.xml (or its Pre/Post version) plus a package.xml through the Metadata API. Change sets can't delete.

flashcards.front: What coverage does RunSpecifiedTests require?
flashcards.back: Each Apex class and trigger in the deployment needs at least 75% coverage from the tests you list.

flashcards.front: How long can you wait to quick deploy a validation?
flashcards.back: Up to 10 days after a successful validation (tests passed, coverage met).

flashcards.front: How do you check that a stubbed method was called?
flashcards.back: The Stub API has no verify(). Record stubbedMethodName and listOfArgs inside handleMethodCall, then assert on what you recorded.

flashcards.front: How do you see real values when the LWC console shows Proxy objects?
flashcards.back: Turn on custom formatters in Chrome DevTools (Console settings). The LWC formatter shows the real values inside the proxies.

questions.q: A new test method queries Accounts and gets zero rows, even though the sandbox has thousands of Accounts. The class has a plain @isTest annotation. What explains this?
options: Sharing rules hide the Accounts, because test methods run as an automated user with no record access
By default, tests can't see existing org data; they must create their own
SOQL is blocked in test methods unless wrapped in Test.startTest()
The query must use ALL ROWS to see records in tests
questions.explain: Tests start with an empty database, so they only see the records they make. Since API 24.0, test methods can't see org data unless the class uses `SeeAllData=true`. Think: a fresh, empty notebook.
wrong: Tests run as the user who started them, in system mode, so sharing isn't the cause.
SOQL works anywhere in a test method, not only inside startTest/stopTest.
`ALL ROWS` adds deleted and archived rows; it doesn't open org data to tests.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Testing Apex - Isolation of Test Data from Organization Data

questions.q: A test class has an @TestSetup method that inserts an Account with Rating = 'Warm'. Test method A updates it to 'Hot'. Test method B then queries the Account and checks Rating. What does B see?
options: 'Hot', because @TestSetup data is shared and committed across methods
An error, because the record was modified by another method
'Warm', because each method gets its own copy of the setup data
It depends on the method execution order, which is alphabetical
questions.explain: Every test method gets its own clean copy of the setup data. Method A's change to 'Hot' rolls back when A ends, so B still sees 'Warm'.
wrong: Setup data isn't shared that way: one method's changes roll back before the next.
No error happens, because each method works on its own copy.
Order doesn't matter, because each method starts from the same clean copy.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Testing Apex - Using Test Setup Methods

questions.q: A test runs without SeeAllData. Which two kinds of existing records can it query without creating them first? (Choose 2)
options: Profile records
Existing Account records
Custom setting records
RecordType records
Existing Case records
questions.explain: A few setup-type objects are always visible, even in an isolated test. `Profile` and `RecordType` are among them, with `User` and `Organization`. Business data and custom setting data stay hidden.
wrong: Accounts are business data, so tests can't see them by default.
Custom setting records count as org data, so the test must insert them.
Cases are business data, so tests can't see them by default.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Testing Apex - Isolation of Test Data from Organization Data

questions.q: An admin maintains a spreadsheet of 30 realistic Accounts that several test classes should use. The developer wants tests to stay independent of org data. What is the best approach?
options: Load the data with Data Loader and use @isTest(SeeAllData=true)
Query the CSV from a Document record inside @TestSetup
Hard-code the Account IDs from the sandbox in the tests
Upload the CSV as a static resource and call Test.loadData
questions.explain: Keep the sample data in a file, and let each test load its own copy. `Test.loadData` inserts the rows of a CSV static resource inside the test. The test stays isolated, and admins can update the file.
wrong: SeeAllData ties tests to org contents, which differ between environments.
Documents are org data, so tests can't see them without SeeAllData.
Record Ids differ between orgs, and tests can't see those records anyway.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Testing Apex - Loading Test Data

questions.q: A method under test runs a SOSL search. In the test, the search always returns no results even though the test inserted matching Contacts. What should the developer do?
options: Call Test.setFixedSearchResults with the IDs the search should return
Add SeeAllData=true so SOSL can use the search index
Call Test.stopTest() before the search so the inserted Contacts get added to the search index
Replace the SOSL in production code with a SOQL LIKE query
questions.explain: SOSL finds nothing in a test unless you tell it what to find. `Test.setFixedSearchResults` sets the Ids the search returns.
wrong: SeeAllData doesn't make SOSL return the test's own records.
stopTest runs queued async jobs; it doesn't add records to the search index.
Changing production code to suit a test is the wrong fix.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Testing Apex - Adding SOSL Queries to Unit Tests

questions.q: What are two effects of wrapping code in Test.startTest() and Test.stopTest()? (Choose 2)
options: The code between them gets a fresh set of governor limits
Records inserted between them are committed to the org
Asynchronous work queued between them runs when stopTest() is called
Validation rules are skipped between them
Callouts made between them are allowed without registering a mock with Test.setMock
questions.explain: startTest and stopTest do two jobs. The code between them gets a fresh set of governor limits. Async work queued between them runs when `stopTest()` is called.
wrong: Test data is never committed to the org; it all rolls back.
Validation rules still run between them.
Callouts still need a mock registered with Test.setMock.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Testing Apex - Using Limits, startTest, and stopTest

questions.q: A test calls Database.executeBatch between Test.startTest() and Test.stopTest(), but its Assert statements are placed right after executeBatch and before stopTest. The assertions fail. What is the fix?
options: Increase the batch scope to 2000
Move the assertions after Test.stopTest()
Call the batch's execute() method twice
Add SeeAllData=true so the job can see its records
questions.explain: A batch queued in a test only runs when the test reaches stopTest. Asserts placed before `Test.stopTest()` check the data before the job ran, so move them after it. Think: stop means go.
wrong: Scope size changes the chunk size, not when the job runs.
Calling execute() by hand skips start() and finish() and isn't needed.
The job can already see the records the test inserted.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Testing Batch Apex

questions.q: An Apex trigger subscribes to Order_Event__e and creates a Task. A test publishes the event with EventBus.publish and immediately queries Tasks, finding none. What should the developer add before the query?
options: A call to System.enqueueJob for the trigger
SeeAllData=true on the test class
A loop that re-queries Tasks until one appears or the CPU time limit is close
Test.getEventBus().deliver() or Test.stopTest()
questions.explain: Events published in a test wait in line until you deliver them. `Test.getEventBus().deliver()` or `Test.stopTest()` sends them to the subscriber trigger, so the Task exists afterwards.
wrong: Event triggers aren't queueable jobs, so enqueueJob doesn't apply.
Data visibility isn't the problem; the event was never delivered.
Apex has no sleep, and waiting never delivers the event; you must force delivery.
questions.source: Platform Events Developer Guide: Testing Your Platform Event in Apex

questions.q: A Schedulable class is scheduled in a test with a cron expression for next January. The test calls System.schedule between Test.startTest() and Test.stopTest(). What happens to the job in the test?
options: It never runs; the test must call execute() directly to cover it
The test waits until the cron time and then times out
Its execute() runs at Test.stopTest(), so its effects can be asserted afterwards
It runs only if the test class has SeeAllData=true
questions.explain: In a test, scheduled jobs don't wait for their clock time. The job's `execute()` runs at `Test.stopTest()`, whatever the cron says, so you can assert right after. You can also query `CronTrigger` to check the schedule.
wrong: The job does run, at stopTest, so calling execute() yourself isn't needed.
Tests never wait for real time to pass.
Scheduling in a test doesn't depend on SeeAllData.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Testing the Apex Scheduler

questions.q: A Queueable job re-enqueues itself to process the next chunk of records. Its test fails with an error when the job tries to chain. What is the documented way to keep the job testable?
options: Guard the chaining call with Test.isRunningTest() and test one link of the chain
Call Test.stopTest() twice to run each chained job
Mark the test with @isTest(SeeAllData=true)
Convert the chain to a for loop inside one execute() call
questions.explain: Chaining a queueable from a test has thrown an error, so the Queueable docs suggest checking `Test.isRunningTest()` before chaining. The test then covers one link of the chain. Current docs also allow testing chains with a suitable maximum stack depth (`AsyncOptions`).
wrong: Only one startTest/stopTest pair is allowed per test method.
SeeAllData has nothing to do with queueable chaining.
One big loop loses the reason to chain: fresh limits for each job.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Queueable Apex

questions.q: A class saved at API version 66.0 is tested to prove that a user without access to the Salary__c field can't read it. Inside System.runAs(limitedUser), a SOQL query in a "with sharing" class returns Salary__c values. Why?
options: runAs only applies to users inserted in @TestSetup, so a user inserted in the test method is ignored
runAs enforces record sharing, not field-level security; the query needs user mode (WITH USER_MODE)
Field-level security is never enforced in tests
The class must be declared inherited sharing, because with sharing ignores the runAs user's access
questions.explain: runAs changes whose records you see, not which fields you may read. At API 66.0, Apex runs in system mode by default, so runAs only adds the user's record sharing. To check field access, the query needs `WITH USER_MODE` or `stripInaccessible`.
wrong: runAs works with any user, wherever it was inserted.
FLS is checked in tests whenever the code enforces it, such as with user mode queries.
Sharing keywords control records, not fields, and with sharing already uses the runAs user.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Using the runAs Method

questions.q: A test inserts a User with a specific Profile and UserRole, then inserts an Account owned by that User, and fails with MIXED_DML_OPERATION. Which two changes fix it? (Choose 2)
options: Wrap the User insert in a System.runAs() block
Insert the User and Account in a single List<SObject>
Use Database.insert with allOrNone set to false
Insert the User from an @future method called inside Test.startTest()/stopTest()
Add SeeAllData=true to the test class
questions.explain: Setup records like Users can't be saved in the same transaction as normal records. In a test, put the User insert inside `System.runAs()` or an `@future` method to split them apart.
wrong: One mixed list still mixes setup and non-setup DML.
Partial success doesn't change the mixed DML rule.
Data visibility has nothing to do with mixed DML.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Setup and Non-Setup Objects in DML

questions.q: A test must prove that OrderService.submit(null) throws OrderService.OrderException. Which pattern makes the test fail if no exception is thrown?
options: Call the method and then Assert.isNull(result)
Wrap the call in try/catch and assert on the exception in catch, with nothing after the call in try
Use Assert.areEqual(OrderException.class, OrderService.submit(null))
Call it in try, then Assert.fail(); in the catch block, assert on the exception
questions.explain: The test needs a line that fails when the exception doesn't come. `Assert.fail()` right after the call only runs if nothing was thrown. The catch block then checks the exception.
wrong: If the exception is thrown, the assert never runs, so this proves nothing.
If nothing is thrown, catch never runs and nothing fails, so the test still passes.
This doesn't compile into a real exception check.
questions.source: Apex Reference Guide: Assert Class

questions.q: A class contains: if (Test.isRunningTest()) { return fakeRate; } else { return callRateApi(); }. Tests pass with 90% coverage, but production keeps failing. Which two statements are true? (Choose 2)
options: The real callout path never runs in tests, so its defects stay hidden
Test.isRunningTest() throws an exception in production orgs
This is the recommended pattern for avoiding callouts in tests
Replacing the branch with an HttpCalloutMock registered via Test.setMock lets tests run the real code path
Branches that use Test.isRunningTest() are excluded from coverage calculations
questions.explain: A test-only branch means tests run different code than production. The real callout path never runs, so its bugs hide behind good coverage. An `HttpCalloutMock` lets the real code run with a fake response.
wrong: It simply returns false in production; nothing is thrown.
The docs recommend callout mocks, not test-only branches.
Those lines count toward coverage like any other code.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Testing HTTP Callouts

questions.q: Which method must a class implement to act as an HttpCalloutMock?
options: HttpResponse respond(HttpRequest req)
void doInvoke(Object stub, Object request, Map<String, Object> response, ...)
Object handleMethodCall(Object stubbedObject, String stubbedMethodName, ...)
HttpRequest send(HttpResponse res)
questions.explain: An HTTP mock has one job: take the request and hand back a fake response. So `HttpCalloutMock` has a single method, `HttpResponse respond(HttpRequest req)`.
wrong: doInvoke belongs to WebServiceMock, the SOAP mock.
handleMethodCall belongs to StubProvider, from the Stub API.
No such method exists, and its types are backwards.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Testing HTTP Callouts by Implementing the HttpCalloutMock Interface

questions.q: A test inserts an Account and then calls a method that makes an HTTP callout. Test.setMock is set, but the test fails with "You have uncommitted work pending". What should the developer change?
options: Use SeeAllData=true so no DML is needed
Replace the HttpCalloutMock with a WebServiceMock, which allows DML before a callout in one transaction
Do the DML before Test.startTest() and make the callout between startTest() and stopTest()
Make the callout from a trigger on Account
questions.explain: In one transaction, you can't save records and then make a callout. Do the DML before `Test.startTest()`, then make the callout between `startTest()` and `stopTest()`. That avoids the uncommitted work error.
wrong: Relying on org data breaks test isolation and isn't the fix.
WebServiceMock is for SOAP and doesn't lift the uncommitted work rule.
Triggers can't make synchronous callouts at all.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Performing DML Operations and Mock Callouts

questions.q: A method calls a rates endpoint and a fees endpoint in the same transaction. The team keeps sample JSON for each in separate static resources. Which mock fits best?
options: StaticResourceCalloutMock
MultiStaticResourceCalloutMock
WebServiceMock
A StubProvider for the Http class
questions.explain: Two endpoints need two different fake answers. `MultiStaticResourceCalloutMock` maps each endpoint to its own static resource, so one mock covers both calls.
wrong: It returns the same single resource for every callout.
WebServiceMock is for SOAP callouts from WSDL2Apex classes.
System types like Http can't be stubbed.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Testing HTTP Callouts Using MultiStaticResourceCalloutMock

questions.q: A developer used WSDL2Apex to generate a SOAP client. How should the test supply a fake response?
options: Implement HttpCalloutMock and return the SOAP envelope XML as the response body from respond()
Use Test.createStub on the generated port class
Set the endpoint to a Remote Site of localhost
Implement WebServiceMock and put the response element into the map with key 'response_x'
questions.explain: WSDL2Apex classes make SOAP callouts, and SOAP callouts need a SOAP mock. Implement `WebServiceMock`, put the reply under `'response_x'`, and register it with `Test.setMock(WebServiceMock.class, ...)`.
wrong: HttpCalloutMock covers callouts made with the Http class, not WSDL2Apex SOAP calls.
The Stub API isn't the documented way to fake WSDL2Apex callouts.
Tests can't make real callouts, not even to localhost.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Test Web Service Callouts

questions.q: A WeatherMock class implementing HttpCalloutMock exists in the org. The test below fails. What is the most likely cause?
options: Callout tests require @isTest(SeeAllData=true)
Test.setMock(HttpCalloutMock.class, new WeatherMock()) is never called, so a real callout is tried
A Remote Site Setting for the endpoint is missing
Assert.areEqual has expected and actual in the wrong order, which makes it fail even on equal values
questions.explain: A mock does nothing until you register it. Without `Test.setMock(HttpCalloutMock.class, new WeatherMock())`, the code tries a real callout, which tests don't allow.
wrong: Callout mocks don't need any org data.
Remote site settings don't matter for mocked callouts; the mock is what's missing.
Swapped arguments only change the failure message, not the result.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Testing HTTP Callouts

questions.q: A developer wants to use the Stub API to replace a dependency in a unit test. Which member of the dependency class can be stubbed?
options: A public static method
A private instance method
A public instance method
A property getter
questions.explain: The Stub API can only swap methods it can reach from outside the object. Public instance methods work, and so do protected and global ones. Static methods, private methods and properties can't be stubbed.
wrong: Static methods can't be stubbed.
Private methods can't be stubbed.
Properties (getters and setters) can't be stubbed.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Build a Mocking Framework with the Stub API

questions.q: How does a test create a stubbed instance of the PricingService class using a StubProvider named PricingStub?
options: (PricingService) Test.createStub(PricingService.class, new PricingStub())
Test.setMock(PricingService.class, new PricingStub())
new PricingService(new PricingStub())
PricingStub.createStub(PricingService.class)
questions.explain: You ask the test system to build the fake, then cast it. `Test.createStub(Type, StubProvider)` returns an Object that you cast to the stubbed type.
wrong: Test.setMock is only for callout mocks.
That just calls the real constructor.
StubProvider has no such static method.
questions.source: Apex Reference Guide: Test.createStub

questions.q: Given the stub provider and test code below, what are the values of d and label?
options: d = 0.25 and label = 'GOLD'
Both are null; stubs need an explicit when() setup
A runtime error, because the provider must return a non-null value for every method
d = 0.25 and label = null
questions.explain: Every call on a stub goes to `handleMethodCall`, and the real methods never run. `getDiscount` matches and returns 0.25. `getTierLabel` falls through to `return null`.
wrong: The real getTierLabel never runs, so nothing returns 'GOLD'.
Apex has no when() API; the provider decides every return value.
Returning null is allowed.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Build a Mocking Framework with the Stub API

questions.q: Where do Lightning Web Component Jest tests run?
options: In the connected org, as part of Apex test runs
In the browser via the Lightning Testing Service only
Locally in Node.js using @salesforce/sfdx-lwc-jest, with no org needed
In a scratch org, during sf project deploy start
questions.explain: Jest is a JavaScript tool that runs on your own computer. LWC Jest tests run locally in Node.js with `@salesforce/sfdx-lwc-jest`. They never touch an org and don't count toward Apex code coverage.
wrong: Jest tests are separate from Apex test runs.
Jest runs in Node with jsdom, not in an org browser session.
Deployments run Apex tests, not Jest.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Test Lightning Web Components

questions.q: The Jest test below fails: the paragraph still shows the old greeting. What should the developer change?
options: Use document.querySelector instead of shadowRoot.querySelector
Make the test async and await Promise.resolve() after setting el.name, then query
Set el.name before calling createElement
Call el.connectedCallback() manually after setting the property, so the template renders again
questions.explain: LWC updates the page a moment later, not right away. After setting `el.name`, `await Promise.resolve()` so the re-render finishes, then check the text.
wrong: Component content lives in the shadow tree, so shadowRoot is right.
Properties are set on the created element; it doesn't exist before createElement.
The engine calls lifecycle hooks itself; the problem is timing.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Write Jest Tests for Lightning Web Components

questions.q: A component uses @wire(getRecord, ...) from lightning/uiRecordApi. How should a Jest test supply record data to the component?
options: Import getRecord in the test and call getRecord.emit(mockData)
Call Test.setMock(getRecord, mockData)
Assign the data to el.record directly from the test
Deploy sample records to a scratch org and run the test with --target-org so the wire gets data
questions.explain: In Jest, wire adapters become test adapters you can push data through. Import `getRecord` and call `getRecord.emit(mockData)` to feed the wired property or function.
wrong: Test.setMock is an Apex method, not JavaScript.
Wired properties are private, so the test can't set them from outside.
Jest tests never use org data.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Test Wire Service

questions.q: A component calls the Apex method AccountController.getAccounts imperatively. Which two steps let a Jest test control its result? (Choose 2)
options: Deploy the Apex class and run the Jest test against the org
Call Test.setMock inside the Jest test file
Use jest.mock on '@salesforce/apex/AccountController.getAccounts' with { virtual: true }, returning { default: jest.fn() }
Register the method as a wire adapter with createLdsTestWireAdapter, then call emit() with the mock data
Use mockResolvedValue or mockRejectedValue on the mocked function to simulate success or an error
questions.explain: Apex imports are fake modules in Jest, so you mock them yourself. Use `jest.mock` with `{ virtual: true }` and a `jest.fn()` default export. Then set `mockResolvedValue` or `mockRejectedValue` for success or an error.
wrong: Jest tests never call real Apex.
Test.setMock is Apex, not JavaScript.
Imperative calls aren't wire adapters, and that helper is deprecated.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Mock Apex Methods in Jest Tests

questions.q: A Visualforce page uses an extension of the Account standard controller and reads the id URL parameter. How should the test set up the controller?
options: Construct the extension with a null StandardController and pass the record id in a public static variable
Use SeeAllData=true, load the page with PageReference.getContent(), then read the extension from it
Call the extension's constructor from an @future method
Call Test.setCurrentPage, add the id to its parameters, then pass new ApexPages.StandardController(acc)
questions.explain: The test must rebuild what a real page visit provides. `Test.setCurrentPage` plus page parameters give the URL context. A `StandardController` wraps the test record for the extension.
wrong: The extension needs a real StandardController, not null.
getContent can't test a controller this way, and tests should make their own data.
No async context is needed to build a controller.
questions.source: Visualforce Developer Guide: Testing Custom Controllers and Controller Extensions

questions.q: The Apex Code log category is set to DEBUG. A statement System.debug(LoggingLevel.FINE, msg) does not appear in the log. Why?
options: FINE is more verbose than DEBUG, so Apex Code must be set to FINE, FINER or FINEST
System.debug only logs messages at ERROR level by default
FINE messages are written only while the Apex Replay Debugger is attached, so they never show in normal logs
The Profiling category must be set to FINE
questions.explain: A debug line shows only if the log level is at least as loud as the line. FINE is louder (more detailed) than DEBUG. So Apex Code must be set to FINE, FINER or FINEST.
wrong: With no level argument, System.debug uses DEBUG, not ERROR.
Replay Debugger only reads logs that already exist; it doesn't change what gets written.
Apex Code, not Profiling, controls System.debug output.
questions.source: Salesforce Help: Debug Log Levels

questions.q: Debug logs for a transaction hit the size limit because a utility class writes thousands of FINEST lines. The developer still needs full detail from OrderService. What should they do?
options: Delete the System.debug statements from the utility class in production
Set the user trace flag to NONE for all categories, so the log only keeps the OrderService output
Add a class trace flag on the utility class with a debug level that sets Apex Code to ERROR
Enable Event Monitoring for Apex execution
questions.explain: You can turn the volume down for one class without muting everyone. A class trace flag overrides the log levels for that class only. Set its Apex Code to ERROR, and the user's flag keeps full detail elsewhere.
wrong: Changing production code just to fix logging is risky and needless.
That would silence OrderService too.
Event Monitoring doesn't control debug log detail.
questions.source: Salesforce Help: Set Up Debug Logging (Trace Flags)

questions.q: A bug only happens in production. The org has no Apex Interactive Debugger sessions. The developer wants to step through the code and inspect variable values. What should they use?
options: Developer Console Query Editor
Apex Replay Debugger in VS Code, using a debug log captured with Apex Code at FINEST
Test.startTest() in Anonymous Apex
Deploy extra System.debug statements with a change set, then step through them in the Developer Console
questions.explain: You can debug production by replaying a log instead of pausing live code. The Apex Replay Debugger in VS Code replays a log captured with Apex Code at FINEST. You get breakpoints, variables and the call stack.
wrong: The Query Editor runs SOQL; it can't step through code.
startTest only works inside test methods.
This changes production code, and the Developer Console can't step through code line by line.
questions.source: Salesforce Extensions for VS Code: Apex Replay Debugger

questions.q: A developer needs to see the heap contents and variable values at a specific line in a deployed class without changing its code. Which two options work? (Choose 2)
options: Set a checkpoint on the line in the Developer Console, run the code, and inspect it in the Checkpoints tab
Add System.debug statements for each variable, deploy them to production, and read the values in the log
Use the Apex Replay Debugger with checkpoints and breakpoints on a captured log
Re-run the test with @isTest(SeeAllData=true)
Call Limits.getHeapSize() from Anonymous Apex
questions.explain: A checkpoint takes a snapshot at a line without touching the code. The Developer Console allows up to 5 checkpoints. The Replay Debugger adds checkpoints to a captured log.
wrong: That needs a code change and a deployment.
Data visibility doesn't show variable values.
It returns one number, not the variables at that line.
questions.source: Salesforce Help: Set Checkpoints in Apex Code

questions.q: A developer wants code to check, at runtime, how many SOQL queries remain before the limit. Which approach is correct?
options: Read the SOQL count from the debug log header
Call System.getQueryCount()
Use Test.getQueries() in production code
Compare Limits.getQueries() with Limits.getLimitQueries()
questions.explain: The `Limits` class tells your code how close it is to each cap. `Limits.getQueries()` is what you've used so far. `Limits.getLimitQueries()` is the max for the context.
wrong: Code can't read its own debug log.
That method doesn't exist.
That method doesn't exist.
questions.source: Apex Reference Guide: Limits Class

questions.q: An Apex class must be removed from production. The team usually deploys with change sets. What should they use?
options: An outbound change set that excludes the class
A Metadata API deployment with destructiveChanges.xml (e.g. via sf CLI)
Delete the class in Setup in production
Rename the class in a sandbox and deploy it with a change set, which replaces the old class
questions.explain: Change sets can only add or update, and production won't let you delete Apex in Setup. A Metadata API deploy with `destructiveChanges.xml`, for example through the sf CLI, removes the class.
wrong: Leaving a class out of a change set doesn't delete it.
Production doesn't allow editing or deleting Apex in Setup.
That adds a second class; the old one stays in production.
questions.source: Metadata API Developer Guide: Deleting Components from an Organization

questions.q: A team wants each developer to work in a short-lived org built from the Git repo, with automatic tracking of local and org changes. What should they use?
options: Scratch orgs created from a Dev Hub
One shared Full sandbox
Change sets between Developer sandboxes
A Partial Copy sandbox per developer
questions.explain: Short-lived orgs built from your repo are exactly what scratch orgs are. They're created from a Dev Hub and track source changes automatically.
wrong: One shared Full sandbox is slow to refresh and not per feature.
Change sets don't track source or use Git.
Partial Copy is for testing with sample data and refreshes only every 5 days.
questions.source: Salesforce DX Developer Guide: Scratch Orgs

questions.q: QA needs an environment with all production metadata plus a representative sample of Accounts and Opportunities chosen by a template. It should be refreshable about weekly. Which sandbox fits?
options: Developer
Developer Pro
Partial Copy
Full
questions.explain: Sample data picked by a template means Partial Copy. It copies all metadata plus template-selected data and can be refreshed every 5 days.
wrong: Developer sandboxes copy no production data.
Developer Pro sandboxes copy no production data either.
Full copies all data and refreshes only every 29 days.
questions.source: Salesforce Help: Sandbox Types and Templates

questions.q: Which two statements about change sets are true? (Choose 2)
options: They can move metadata between any two Salesforce orgs
The target org must authorize a deployment connection from the source org
They can delete components in the target org
They can't delete components; destructive changes need the Metadata API
They automatically add every dependent component
questions.explain: Change sets are a simple tool with tight limits. They only move between orgs tied to the same production org, and they need a deployment connection. They only add or update components.
wrong: They only work between orgs tied to the same production org.
Change sets can't delete anything.
You add dependencies yourself, with help from "View/Add Dependencies".
questions.source: Salesforce Help: Change Sets

questions.q: A CI job creates an unlocked package version and then runs sf package version promote, which fails. Tests pass locally. What is the most likely cause?
options: Unlocked packages can't contain Apex
The package has no namespace
The Dev Hub must be a sandbox
The version was created without --code-coverage, or its coverage is below 75%
questions.explain: A package version can be promoted only if its coverage was measured and is high enough. That means creating it with `--code-coverage` and reaching at least 75%.
wrong: Unlocked packages can include Apex.
Unlocked packages can be created without a namespace.
A Dev Hub is a production or Developer Edition org, never a sandbox.
questions.source: Salesforce DX Developer Guide: Release an Unlocked Package

questions.q: A deployment to production includes Apex classes, and no test level is specified. Which tests run by default?
options: All local tests (RunLocalTests)
No tests (NoTestRun)
All tests including managed packages (RunAllTestsInOrg)
Only tests named like the deployed classes
questions.explain: Production won't take Apex without running tests. With no test level set, it uses `RunLocalTests`: every test except those from installed managed and unlocked packages.
wrong: NoTestRun is the default only for non-production orgs.
Managed package tests aren't included by default.
No test level matches tests by name.
questions.source: Metadata API Developer Guide: Running Tests in a Deployment

questions.q: A developer deploys ClassA and ClassB to production with RunSpecifiedTests and two test classes. ClassA reaches 90% coverage, ClassB 60%. Org-wide coverage would be 85%. What happens?
options: It succeeds because org-wide coverage is above 75%
It succeeds because RunSpecifiedTests skips coverage checks
It fails because each deployed class needs 75% coverage from the specified tests
It succeeds, but ClassB is deployed as inactive
questions.explain: With RunSpecifiedTests, each piece is graded on its own. Every class and trigger in the deployment needs 75% coverage from the listed tests. ClassB at 60% fails, whatever the org average.
wrong: Org-wide coverage isn't what RunSpecifiedTests checks.
Coverage is still checked, for each component.
Apex classes have no inactive state.
questions.source: Metadata API Developer Guide: Running a Subset of Tests in a Deployment

questions.q: A release manager validated a production deployment on Monday and wants to deploy it on Thursday without re-running tests. Which two conditions must be met for quick deploy? (Choose 2)
options: The validation succeeded within the last 10 days
Apex tests passed and the coverage requirements were met during validation
The validation used NoTestRun
The validation targeted a sandbox instead of production
All deployed classes were created by the same user
questions.explain: Quick deploy reuses a passing validation, so that validation must be recent and complete. It must have succeeded against the same org within 10 days, with tests passed and coverage met.
wrong: With no tests run, there's nothing to reuse for Apex.
The validation must target the org you deploy to.
Who wrote the classes doesn't matter.
questions.source: Salesforce Help: Quick Deploy

questions.q: A pricing team's test class creates a Gold tier once in @TestSetup and keeps its Id in a static variable so every test method can reuse it. appliesGoldDiscount fails because the service returns a discount of 0. What is the cause?
options: The Tier__c record is rolled back before appliesGoldDiscount runs, so the tier no longer exists
@TestSetup records can only be read by test methods annotated @IsTest(SeeAllData=true) at method level
goldTierId is null: statics set in @TestSetup reset for each test method. Query the tier instead
Test.startTest() resets all static variables, so goldTierId must be assigned after it
questions.explain: Each test method starts fresh, and so do static variables. Statics set in `@TestSetup` are null again in every test method. The Tier__c record still exists, so query it, for example by Name.
wrong: Setup records stay for every test method; only each method's own changes roll back.
Setup records are visible by default, and @TestSetup isn't even allowed with SeeAllData=true.
startTest gives fresh governor limits; it doesn't reset variables.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Using Test Setup Methods

questions.q: A team is refactoring 30 test classes to share data through @TestSetup methods. During code review, which two statements about test setup methods are correct? (Choose 2)
options: A class annotated @IsTest(SeeAllData=true) at class level can still use @TestSetup to add extra records
If the @TestSetup method throws an exception or an assertion fails, the whole class fails and no test methods run
A class can have one @TestSetup method for each sObject type it seeds
Non-test methods called from the @TestSetup method get no code coverage from that call
Updates that one test method makes to setup records are visible to the test methods that run after it
questions.explain: Test setup is all or nothing, and it earns no coverage. If `@TestSetup` throws or an assert fails, the whole class fails, and code it calls gets no coverage from that call. Only one setup method is allowed per class.
wrong: Test setup methods aren't allowed in a class with access to org data.
Only one test setup method is allowed per test class.
Changes made by a test method roll back when that method ends.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Using Test Setup Methods

questions.q: A CPQ developer tests a quote line calculator. The test below throws System.QueryException: List has no rows for assignment to SObject on the marked line, although the sandbox has an active standard price book. What should the developer change?
options: Use Test.getStandardPricebookId() for Pricebook2Id instead of querying the standard price book
Insert a new Pricebook2 with IsStandard = true earlier in the test
Add @IsTest(IsParallel=true) so the test can read shared reference data
Move the query into an @TestSetup method, which can see org data
questions.explain: Tests can't see the org's standard price book, but they can get its Id. `Test.getStandardPricebookId()` returns it, so the test can create standard PricebookEntry records.
wrong: IsStandard can't be set, so a test can't make a second standard price book.
IsParallel doesn't open data access, and parallel tests can't call getStandardPricebookId().
@TestSetup methods have the same data isolation as test methods.
questions.source: Apex Reference Guide: Test Class (getStandardPricebookId)

questions.q: A legacy test class depends on org data. A developer adds a new method and wants only that method isolated from org data. In a sandbox with 5,000 Accounts, what does the query in isolatedCount return?
options: 1, because the method-level SeeAllData=false overrides the class annotation
0, because SeeAllData=false also hides the records the test inserts
It doesn't compile, because a method annotation can't contradict the class annotation
5,001, because SeeAllData=false on a method is ignored when its class has SeeAllData=true
questions.explain: A method can open data access, but it can't close what its class opened. With the class at `SeeAllData=true`, a method's `SeeAllData=false` is ignored. So it sees all 5,000 Accounts plus the one it inserted.
wrong: The override only works one way: a method's true overrides a class's false.
Tests always see the records they create.
It compiles; the method annotation is just ignored.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Using the isTest(SeeAllData=True) Annotation

questions.q: To speed up CI runs, a developer marks an invoicing test class as parallel. The test now fails before it reaches its assertion. What is the reason?
options: Queueable jobs started from a test need @IsTest(SeeAllData=true)
Parallel tests (IsParallel=true) can't call System.enqueueJob(). Remove IsParallel or move the test
Test.startTest() and Test.stopTest() aren't allowed in parallel test classes
System.enqueueJob() must be called before Test.startTest() in a parallel class so the job is queued in time
questions.explain: Parallel tests trade speed for a few banned calls. `IsParallel=true` tests can't call `System.enqueueJob()`, `System.schedule()` or `Test.getStandardPricebookId()`. This test must run without IsParallel.
wrong: Queueable jobs don't need org data access.
startTest and stopTest work in parallel tests; the ban is on enqueueJob.
The job must be queued inside startTest/stopTest so it runs at stopTest.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: IsTest Annotation

questions.q: A nightly batch class recalculates Account health scores. Its test inserts 400 Accounts and fails at Test.stopTest() with an error saying no more than one executeBatch can be called from within a test method. Which two changes fix the error? (Choose 2)
options: Call Test.stopTest() a second time to run the second chunk
Annotate the test with @IsTest(SeeAllData=true)
Insert 200 or fewer Accounts (and adjust the assertion) so the default scope needs one execute() call
Move Database.executeBatch() above Test.startTest()
Pass a scope that covers all records: Database.executeBatch(new HealthScoreBatch(), 400)
questions.explain: A test can run a batch's `execute()` only once. With the default scope of 200, 400 records need two chunks. Use fewer records, or raise the scope so every record fits in one chunk.
wrong: stopTest can be called only once per test method.
Org data access doesn't change how many execute() calls a test allows.
Outside startTest/stopTest, the batch doesn't finish before the assertion.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Using Batch Apex

questions.q: A trigger on Order_Event__e creates a Shipment__c and publishes a Shipment_Event__e. A second trigger, on Shipment_Event__e, inserts a Notification__c. The test below finds the Shipment__c but no Notification__c. What should the developer add?
options: Replace EventBus.publish with Database.insert, because tests can't publish platform events
Annotate the test with SeeAllData=true so the second trigger is subscribed
Call Test.getEventBus().deliver() again before the Notification__c assertion
Call Test.stopTest() a second time right after the first deliver()
questions.explain: Each `deliver()` sends only the events waiting at that moment. The first trigger publishes Shipment_Event__e during the first delivery. So call `Test.getEventBus().deliver()` again before checking for the Notification__c.
wrong: EventBus.publish is the supported way to publish events in tests.
Event triggers subscribe in tests without org data access.
stopTest can be called only once per test method.
questions.source: Platform Events Developer Guide: Deliver Test Event Messages

questions.q: A batch class implements Database.RaisesPlatformEvents, and a BatchApexErrorEvent trigger writes failures to Error_Log__c. The test forces a failure in execute(), but it fails at Test.stopTest() and never reaches the assertion. Which two changes make the test work as intended? (Choose 2)
options: Wrap the startTest/executeBatch/stopTest block in try/catch, because the batch exception is passed to the test method
Annotate the test with @IsTest(SeeAllData=true) so BatchApexErrorEvent triggers run
Call Test.getEventBus().deliver() before Database.executeBatch()
After that block, call Test.getEventBus().deliver() to deliver the BatchApexErrorEvent, then assert
Replace Test.stopTest() with Test.getEventBus().deliver(), which also runs the queued batch and its error event
questions.explain: In a test, a batch job's exception is passed up to the test method. Catch it around the startTest/executeBatch/stopTest block. The BatchApexErrorEvent still waits on the test bus, so call `Test.getEventBus().deliver()` before asserting.
wrong: Event triggers don't need org data access.
Nothing is published yet; the event is published when the batch fails.
deliver() delivers event messages; it doesn't run queued batch jobs.
questions.source: Platform Events Developer Guide: Deliver Test Event Messages

questions.q: A developer logs governor usage in a test while investigating a limit problem. The test runs synchronously. What are the values of a and b?
questions.explain: startTest opens a fresh limits counter, and stopTest brings the old one back. Inside the block, only the Contact query counts, so a is 1. After stopTest, the earlier count returns, so b is 3.
wrong: startTest begins new limits, so the first 3 queries don't count in a.
After stopTest, the old limits return without the query from inside the block.
The Contact query ran after startTest, so a is 1.
questions.source: Apex Reference Guide: Test Class (startTest, stopTest)

questions.q: A test builds a support agent User but the developer forgot to insert it before calling System.runAs. What happens when the test runs?
options: System.runAs throws an exception because the User has no Id
The block runs as the original test user, because runAs ignores users that aren't inserted
It doesn't compile, because runAs only accepts a User Id
runAs inserts the User implicitly, and the code in the block runs as that new user
questions.explain: runAs is forgiving with new users. If the User isn't inserted yet, runAs inserts it and runs the block as that user. It also ignores user license limits.
wrong: runAs inserts the new User instead of failing.
The block runs as the User passed in, not the original user.
runAs takes a User record (or a package Version), not an Id.
questions.source: Apex Reference Guide: System Class (runAs)

questions.q: A territory test (API version 60.0) must create a sales rep User and Accounts in the same test method. Which two approaches avoid a MIXED_DML_OPERATION error? (Choose 2)
options: Insert the User with UserRoleId left null, then insert an Account owned by that User
Insert the User with a UserRoleId, then insert the Account, with both statements directly in the test method
Insert the Account first, then insert the User with a UserRoleId inside System.runAs(new User(Id = UserInfo.getUserId()))
Update an Account, then update a User's ProfileId, both directly in the test method
Insert the User with a UserRoleId and the Account in one call to Database.insert(records, false)
questions.explain: Users with a role are setup data that can't mix with normal records. Since API 15.0, a User with a null `UserRoleId` is exempt. When a role is needed, put the setup DML in a `System.runAs` block.
wrong: A User with a role plus an Account in one transaction is mixed DML.
Changing a User's ProfileId alongside non-setup DML is mixed DML.
Partial success doesn't lift the mixed DML rule.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: sObjects That Can't Be Used Together in DML Operations

questions.q: A reviewer says this test can never fail, because catch (Exception e) will swallow the failure thrown by Assert.fail(). What actually happens if OrderService.submit(null) does NOT throw?
options: The test passes, because the catch block catches the AssertException
The test fails at Assert.fail(), because a failed assertion can't be caught by a catch block
The test fails inside the catch block, because isInstanceOfType rejects the caught AssertException
It doesn't compile, because Assert.fail() can't appear inside a try block
questions.explain: A failed assertion can't be caught, just like a LimitException. So `catch (Exception e)` never runs, and the test fails with the `Assert.fail()` message.
wrong: Failed assertions can't be caught, so the catch block never runs.
The catch block never runs for a failed assertion.
Assert.fail() is valid anywhere in a method.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Exception Statements

questions.q: A permission test checks that each of 160 users, spread over several profiles, can update Accounts. The users are inserted with one DML statement before the loop. The test fails with System.LimitException: Too many DML statements: 151. Why?
options: Each call to System.runAs counts against the DML statement limit
runAs inserts each User again, and every insert counts as a DML statement
Describe calls such as isUpdateable() count as DML statements
System.runAs can't be used inside a loop; it must wrap the whole loop
questions.explain: Every `System.runAs` call counts as a DML statement. Two inserts plus 149 runAs calls reach the limit of 150, so the next call fails. Test fewer users per method, or split them across methods.
wrong: These users were already inserted, so runAs doesn't insert them again.
Describe calls don't count as DML.
runAs works inside loops; the problem is the DML count.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Using the runAs Method

questions.q: A shipping integration calls a rates endpoint and then a labels endpoint inside ShippingService.buyLabel(). The team stores a sample response for each endpoint in its own static resource. The test below fails because buyLabel() returns null: the labels call can't parse the response it gets. Which change fixes the test?
options: Put both JSON bodies in the RatesResponse static resource
Register a second StaticResourceCalloutMock with the LabelResponse resource right before calling buyLabel()
Use MultiStaticResourceCalloutMock, map each endpoint to its resource, and register it with Test.setMock
Replace setStaticResource with setBody on the mock, because static resources can't be read from test methods
questions.explain: A single-resource mock gives every callout the same answer. `StaticResourceCalloutMock` sends the rates JSON to the labels call too. `MultiStaticResourceCalloutMock` gives each endpoint its own static resource.
wrong: The mock still returns one body to both calls, so neither gets what it expects.
Both calls happen inside buyLabel(), so one single-resource mock answers both.
Tests can read static resources; that's how these mocks work.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Testing HTTP Callouts Using Static Resources

questions.q: A developer writes one reusable mock so a test can fake several endpoints. The class fails to save. What is wrong?
options: respond() must take exactly one HttpRequest parameter. Read the path from req.getEndpoint() instead
A mock class can't be annotated @IsTest
Mock classes can't have constructors that take parameters
respond() must be declared global, so the mock class itself must be global rather than public to save
questions.explain: An interface method must match its signature exactly. `HttpCalloutMock` needs `HttpResponse respond(HttpRequest req)`, with one parameter. Read the path from `req.getEndpoint()` instead.
wrong: Mock classes are often @IsTest so they don't count toward the code size limit.
A constructor with parameters is fine; the test passes the values in.
The class implementing HttpCalloutMock can be public or global.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Testing HTTP Callouts by Implementing the HttpCalloutMock Interface

questions.q: A developer is mocking a SOAP service whose client classes were generated with WSDL2Apex. Which two statements about the WebServiceMock implementation are correct? (Choose 2)
options: doInvoke returns the generated response element, which the runtime passes to the client
doInvoke puts the generated response element into the response map under the key 'response_x'
The mock is registered with Test.setMock(HttpCalloutMock.class, new MySoapMock())
The mock class must implement both WebServiceMock and HttpCalloutMock, because SOAP calls are sent over HTTP
The mock class can be public and annotated @IsTest so it doesn't count toward the code size limit
questions.explain: A SOAP mock doesn't return its answer; it drops it in a map. `doInvoke` is void and puts the response element under `'response_x'`. The class can be public and `@IsTest`, which keeps it out of the 6 MB code size limit.
wrong: doInvoke is void; the reply goes into the response map.
SOAP mocks are registered with WebServiceMock.class.
WebServiceMock alone covers WSDL2Apex callouts.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Test Web Service Callouts

questions.q: A Queueable that implements Database.AllowsCallouts sends invoices to an ERP system. Its test fails with an error saying test methods don't support callouts. What is the fix?
