options: Move the insert after Test.startTest(), so uncommitted work doesn't block the callout when the job runs
Add Database.AllowsCallouts to the test class as well, so its test methods are allowed to make callouts
Call Test.setMock inside the Queueable's execute() method
Call Test.setMock before Test.stopTest(), ideally before enqueuing, because the job runs at stopTest
questions.explain: The mock must be in place before the job runs. The queued job runs at `Test.stopTest()`, so register the mock before then, ideally before enqueuing.
wrong: DML before startTest is the recommended order and isn't the cause here.
AllowsCallouts marks async classes, not test classes.
Test setup doesn't belong in production code; the test registers the mock.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Queueable Apex; Testing HTTP Callouts by Implementing the HttpCalloutMock Interface

questions.q: An architect plans to replace slow dependencies with Test.createStub() across a service layer. Which two of these classes can NOT be stubbed with the Stub API? (Choose 2)
options: AccountCleanupBatch, which implements Database.Batchable<SObject>
PricingService, a public top-level class with a public no-argument constructor
TaxCalculator, a public virtual class whose methods return Map<String, Object>
RegistryService, a top-level class whose only constructor is private
ShippingClient, a public top-level class in the same namespace as the test
questions.explain: The Stub API needs a class it can build and extend from outside. It can't mock Batchable classes or classes with only private constructors. It also can't mock static or private methods, properties, triggers, inner classes or system types.
wrong: A public top-level class with an accessible constructor can be stubbed.
Map return types are fine; only iterators can't be used as return or parameter types.
A class in the same namespace as the createStub call can be stubbed.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Build a Mocking Framework with the Stub API

questions.q: CatalogService has two overloads, Decimal getPrice(String) and Decimal getPrice(String, Integer), plus Boolean isActive(String). Given the stub provider and test code below, what are a, b and c?
options: a = 10, b = 30, c = true
a = 1.5, b = 1.5, c = false
a = 1.5, b = 30, c = null
a = null, b = 30, c = null
questions.explain: Every call on the stub goes to `handleMethodCall`, which checks its branches in order. The two-argument overload hits the first branch (10 × 3 = 30). The one-argument call falls to the Decimal branch (1.5), and isActive gets null.
wrong: The real methods never run, and nothing in the provider returns true.
The two-argument call hits the first branch, and null isn't turned into false.
The one-argument call matches the Decimal return-type branch.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Build a Mocking Framework with the Stub API

questions.q: An ISV team writes its tests in its own namespace, acme. They want Test.createStub() to stub a service class from a partner's managed package (namespace ptnr), and they keep their StubProvider in a shared utility package with a third namespace. What is true?
options: It works, as long as the partner's class is global and virtual
It fails: the stubbed class must be in the test's namespace; the StubProvider can be in any namespace
It fails: the StubProvider must be in the same namespace as the stubbed class; the test can be anywhere
It works only if the test is annotated @IsTest(SeeAllData=true)
questions.explain: The stubbed class must live in the same namespace as the `Test.createStub()` call. The StubProvider can live in any namespace. So stubbing the partner's class from acme fails.
wrong: Being global doesn't lift the namespace rule.
It's the other way around: the stubbed class must match the test, and the provider can be anywhere.
Data access has nothing to do with stubbing.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Build a Mocking Framework with the Stub API

questions.q: A productCard component uses @wire(getRecord). The Jest test below fails because the .name element is empty. What is the most likely fix?
options: Append the element to the DOM before calling getRecord.emit(); wire data only reaches a connected component
Replace await Promise.resolve() with jest.runAllTimers()
Register the adapter with registerLdsTestWireAdapter(getRecord) before emitting, so emit() reaches the component
Query document.querySelector('.name') instead of using the shadowRoot
questions.explain: A component only gets wire data once it's on the page. Emitting before `appendChild` sends the data to no one. Append first, then emit, then await a promise before checking.
wrong: The re-render is a microtask, not a timer, so awaiting a resolved promise is right.
Current sfdx-lwc-jest doesn't need registration, and the element must still be connected first.
Elements inside the component are reachable only through element.shadowRoot.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Write Jest Tests for Lightning Web Components That Use the Wire Service

questions.q: In contactTile, clicking the link runs this.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('select', { detail: this.contact.Id })). The test below fails because the handler is never called. What should change?
options: Make the test async and await Promise.resolve() before clicking
Dispatch the event with bubbles: true and composed: true so the test can receive it
Use dispatchEvent(new MouseEvent('click')) instead of click()
Listen for 'select', not 'onselect'. The on prefix is only used for handlers in a parent's template
questions.explain: A listener must use the event's exact name. The event was dispatched as `'select'`, so listen for `'select'`. The `onselect` form is only for handlers in a parent's HTML.
wrong: The listener name never matches, so waiting doesn't help.
The test listens on the host element, which gets the event without bubbling.
click() already fires a click event on the link.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Create and Dispatch Events; Test Lightning Web Components

questions.q: A Jest test for a refresh button throws TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'click'). The component template contains <lightning-button label="Refresh" onclick={handleRefresh}>. What is wrong?
options: Base components like lightning-button aren't rendered in Jest, so the test must click a native button instead
The button is in the component's shadow tree, so find it with element.shadowRoot.querySelector()
The test must await a promise before appendChild() so the template renders
document.querySelector only works after jest.useFakeTimers() is called
questions.explain: What a component renders lives inside its shadow tree. Page-level queries like `document.querySelector` can't see in there. Use `element.shadowRoot.querySelector()`.
wrong: sfdx-lwc-jest supplies stubs for base components, so lightning-button is there to click.
The first render happens on appendChild; nothing needs awaiting before it.
Timers have nothing to do with DOM queries.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: DOM Inspection Tests Are Subject to Change; Test Lightning Web Components

questions.q: A component uses @wire(getContactList), imported from '@salesforce/apex/ContactController.getContactList'. The test below throws TypeError: getContactList.emit is not a function. What should the jest.mock factory return?
options: { default: jest.fn().mockResolvedValue(mockContacts) }
Keep the factory as it is and call getContactList.mockResolvedValue(mockContacts) in the test instead of emit()
{ default: createApexTestWireAdapter(jest.fn()) }, with the helper required from '@salesforce/sfdx-lwc-jest'
{ emit: jest.fn() }, so the test can spy on emit
questions.explain: Wired Apex needs a wire adapter mock, not a plain function. Make the default export `createApexTestWireAdapter(jest.fn())`, which gives you `emit()` and `error()`. A plain `jest.fn()` only suits imperative calls.
wrong: A resolved promise is for imperative calls, and this mock still has no emit().
The component never calls a wired method as a promise, so the value never arrives.
The component imports the default export, so that export must be the wire adapter.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Write Jest Tests for Lightning Web Components That Use the Wire Service (lwc-recipes apexWireMethodToProperty test)

questions.q: A developer must prove that accountHeader passes its recordId and the right fields to getRecord, without checking the DOM. NAME_FIELD is imported from @salesforce/schema in both files. Which assertion does this?
options: expect(getRecord.getLastConfig()).toEqual({ recordId: '001xx000003DGb2AAG', fields: [NAME_FIELD] })
expect(getRecord).toHaveBeenCalledWith('001xx000003DGb2AAG')
expect(element.account.data.id).toBe('001xx000003DGb2AAG')
expect(getRecord.emit).toHaveBeenCalledWith({ recordId: '001xx000003DGb2AAG' })
questions.explain: Test wire adapters remember the settings the component sent them. `getLastConfig()` returns the latest config, with `'$recordId'` already replaced by the real Id.
wrong: The component doesn't call the adapter like a function, so call checks don't apply.
account isn't public, so the test can't read it, and no data was emitted.
emit() is what the test calls to push data; it doesn't record the config.
questions.source: sfdx-lwc-jest test wire adapters (lwc-recipes apexWireMethodWithParams test)

questions.q: A Visualforce controller extension catches a DmlException in save() and calls ApexPages.addMessages(e). The test below forces the failure. Which assertion best proves that the user would see an error on the page?
options: Assert.isNull(next), because a null PageReference always means an error message was shown
Assert.isTrue(ApexPages.hasMessages(ApexPages.Severity.ERROR))
Assert.areEqual(1, [SELECT COUNT() FROM ApexPageMessage__c])
Assert.isTrue(Test.isRunningTest())
questions.explain: Check the messages the page would show, not a side effect. `ApexPages.hasMessages(ApexPages.Severity.ERROR)` proves an error was added. `ApexPages.getMessages()` reads the messages.
wrong: A null return just keeps the user on the page; it doesn't prove a message.
Page messages aren't saved as records.
That only proves the code runs in a test.
questions.source: Apex Reference Guide: ApexPages Class

questions.q: Users report a JavaScript error in a Lightning web component in a sandbox. In the browser's developer tools, the framework and component code is minified and hard to follow. Which two actions help the developer debug the component's JavaScript? (Choose 2)
options: Set the Apex Code log level to FINEST for the user
Enable Debug Mode for the developer's user in Setup so Lightning JavaScript isn't minified
Run the component's Jest tests against the sandbox with --target-org
Open a downloaded debug log in Apex Replay Debugger to step through the component's JavaScript
Add a debugger statement or set a breakpoint in the browser's Sources panel, then reproduce the issue
questions.explain: To debug browser JavaScript, make it readable and then pause it. Debug Mode serves Lightning JavaScript unminified. A breakpoint or `debugger` statement then pauses the code in the browser's developer tools.
wrong: Debug logs cover server-side code, not JavaScript in the browser.
Jest tests run locally in Node.js and never connect to an org.
Replay Debugger replays Apex from logs, not browser JavaScript.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Debug Lightning Web Components; Salesforce Help: Enable Debug Mode for Lightning Components

questions.q: An import utility logs its failures to a custom object. During a large import, users get an error and no Import_Log__c record is written, and the debug log shows no "Import finished" line. What explains this?
options: The catch block runs, but its insert is rolled back because DML inside a try statement only commits on success
A QueryException is thrown first, and catch (Exception e) can't catch it
The 101st query throws System.LimitException, which can't be caught, so the whole transaction rolls back
The finally block runs first and ends the transaction before catch can log
questions.explain: Hitting a governor limit is a crash you can't catch. The 101st query throws `System.LimitException`, so catch and finally don't run and the transaction rolls back. Bulkify the query, or check `Limits.getQueries()` first.
wrong: For catchable exceptions, the catch block runs and its DML commits.
QueryException is catchable with catch (Exception e).
finally runs after catch, and it doesn't end the transaction.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Exception Statements

questions.q: A support engineer chasing an intermittent bug leaves FINEST logging on for an integration user that runs all day. Which two statements about debug log limits are correct? (Choose 2)
options: A log larger than 20 MB is reduced by removing older log lines, which can come from anywhere in the log
A log larger than 20 MB is discarded completely and replaced by a single entry saying the log was too large
While the Developer Console is open, debug logs are generated for every user in the org
If more than 1,000 MB of debug logs is generated in 15 minutes, trace flags are disabled
System debug logs are kept for 30 days
questions.explain: Debug logs have size and time caps. A log over 20 MB is trimmed by removing older lines, and over 1,000 MB of logs in 15 minutes switches trace flags off. System debug logs are kept for 24 hours.
wrong: The log is trimmed, not thrown away.
The Developer Console records logs only for its own user.
System debug logs are kept for 24 hours; monitoring debug logs for seven days.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Debug Log

questions.q: An integration user calls OrderService through a REST endpoint. To get detail from that class only, a developer adds an Apex class trace flag on OrderService with Apex Code set to FINEST, then waits. No debug logs appear for the integration calls. What should the developer do?
options: Add System = FINEST to the class trace flag's debug level
Add a trigger trace flag on every trigger that OrderService fires
Keep the Developer Console open while the calls run, because it records logs for every user while it's open
Add a user trace flag for the integration user; class trace flags don't start logging on their own
questions.explain: A class trace flag sets the detail, but it doesn't switch logging on. A user trace flag on the integration user starts the logs. The class flag then sets the detail for OrderService.
wrong: More categories on the class flag still don't start logging.
Trigger trace flags don't start logs on their own either.
The Developer Console records logs only for its own user.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Debug Log

questions.q: After a release, updating 120 Opportunities with Data Loader fails. The developer pulls this excerpt from the debug log. What is the root cause?
questions.code:
13:02:11.204 (204511000)|CODE_UNIT_STARTED|[EXTERNAL]|01qxx0000004C9z|OpportunityTrigger on Opportunity trigger event AfterUpdate
13:02:11.209 (209881000)|SOQL_EXECUTE_BEGIN|[14]|Aggregations:0|SELECT Id, Rating FROM Account WHERE Id = :tmpVar1
13:02:11.212 (212004000)|SOQL_EXECUTE_END|[14]|Rows:1
13:02:11.215 (215120000)|SOQL_EXECUTE_BEGIN|[14]|Aggregations:0|SELECT Id, Rating FROM Account WHERE Id = :tmpVar1
13:02:11.217 (217337000)|SOQL_EXECUTE_END|[14]|Rows:1
... the same pair repeats, always at line [14] ...
13:02:11.871 (871220000)|EXCEPTION_THROWN|[14]|System.LimitException: Too many SOQL queries: 101
13:02:11.871 (871390000)|FATAL_ERROR|System.LimitException: Too many SOQL queries: 101
options: Data Loader sends 1,000 records per trigger call, which lowers the query limit
Line 14 runs an Account query per Opportunity inside a loop. Query once with a set of Ids before it
The Account query isn't selective, so it times out and is retried automatically until the SOQL limit is hit
The trigger should catch the LimitException and retry the remaining records in a Queueable
questions.explain: The same line running the same query again and again means a query inside a loop. Every SOQL_EXECUTE_BEGIN comes from line [14], with one row each time. Query once with `WHERE Id IN :accountIds` before the loop.
wrong: Triggers get records in chunks of up to 200, and the limit stays the same.
Each query returns one row in milliseconds; nothing times out.
LimitException can't be caught.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Debug Log; Execution Governors and Limits

questions.q: A nightly batch job should create a follow-up Task for each Opportunity. The job completes, no exception appears in the debug log, but many Tasks are missing. What is the most likely cause?
options: With allOrNone false, failed records are returned in SaveResults instead of throwing, and nobody checks them
Tasks inserted in execute() are held until finish() runs, and they're dropped if finish() doesn't commit them
DML in execute() is deferred to the next execute() call, so records from the last chunk are never saved
WhatId can't be set from Apex, so those Tasks are skipped
questions.explain: With `allOrNone` set to false, failures don't throw; they hide in the results. Failed records, for example ones with an inactive owner, appear only in the returned `Database.SaveResult` list. Check `isSuccess()` and log `getErrors()`.
wrong: Records inserted in execute() commit when that execute() transaction ends.
DML isn't held over between execute() calls.
Apex can set WhatId on a Task.
questions.source: Apex Reference Guide: Database Class; SaveResult Class

questions.q: A CI script builds an unlocked package version. The pipeline owner wants fast builds, but the version must be promotable to released. The command below fails right away. Why?
questions.code:
sf package version create \
  --package "Billing Core" \
  --installation-key-bypass \
  --skip-validation \
  --code-coverage \
  --wait 30
options: --installation-key-bypass can't be used with unlocked packages, so the version needs an --installation-key
--skip-validation can't be combined with --code-coverage, and skip-validation versions can't be promoted
--wait must be at least 60 minutes when --code-coverage is set
Unlocked packages compute coverage at promote time, so --code-coverage isn't a valid flag
questions.explain: Coverage is measured during validation, so you can't skip one and keep the other. `--skip-validation` and `--code-coverage` can't be combined. Versions built with skip validation also can't be promoted.
wrong: Installation key bypass is valid for unlocked packages.
There's no minimum wait time.
Coverage is measured at version creation with --code-coverage, and promotion needs it.
questions.source: Salesforce DX Developer Guide: Create New Versions of an Unlocked Package; Code Coverage for Unlocked Packages

questions.q: A release manager is planning environments for a regulated insurer. Which two statements about sandboxes are correct? (Choose 2)
options: A Developer sandbox includes a sample of production data chosen by a sandbox template
A Partial Copy sandbox copies all production data but no metadata
A Developer Pro sandbox can be refreshed once a day
Refreshing a sandbox keeps the sandbox's own changes and adds production's new metadata
A Full sandbox can be refreshed every 29 days
questions.explain: Each sandbox type has its own refresh interval. Developer and Developer Pro refresh every day, and Full every 29 days. Only Partial Copy and Full sandboxes copy production data.
wrong: Developer sandboxes copy metadata only; templates are for Partial Copy and Full.
Partial Copy copies all metadata plus a template-picked sample of data.
A refresh replaces the sandbox with a new copy, so its own changes are lost.
questions.source: Salesforce Help: Sandbox Types and Templates

questions.q: A release pipeline must read per-class coverage after tests run in a sandbox, to block merges below 85%. The command below fails with sObject type 'ApexCodeCoverageAggregate' is not supported. What is the fix?
questions.code:
sf data query \
  --query "SELECT ApexClassOrTrigger.Name, NumLinesCovered, NumLinesUncovered FROM ApexCodeCoverageAggregate" \
  --target-org uat
options: Add --use-tooling-api, because ApexCodeCoverageAggregate is a Tooling API object
Retrieve ApexCodeCoverageAggregate with sf project retrieve start, because it is Metadata API metadata
Run the query in Execute Anonymous, because coverage records are only visible from Apex
Query a coverage field on ApexClass through the standard API instead
questions.explain: Coverage records live in the Tooling API, not the standard API. `ApexCodeCoverageAggregate` is a Tooling API object, so `sf data query` needs `--use-tooling-api`.
wrong: Coverage results aren't metadata, so they can't be retrieved.
Apex SOQL can't query Tooling API objects.
ApexClass has no coverage field; coverage lives in Tooling API objects.
questions.source: Tooling API Developer Guide: ApexCodeCoverageAggregate; Salesforce CLI Command Reference: data query

questions.q: A team that relies heavily on admins is moving from change sets to DevOps Center. Which statement describes how DevOps Center manages changes?
options: It packages each work item into an outbound change set and uploads it to the next connected org in the pipeline
It requires every developer to work in scratch orgs created from a Dev Hub
Work items are committed to a source control repository and promoted through pipeline stages
It lets work items skip Apex tests when they are promoted to production
questions.explain: DevOps Center is built on source control. Each work item's changes are committed to a repository and promoted through pipeline stages, instead of moving by change set.
wrong: DevOps Center replaces change sets with promotion based on source control.
Sandboxes work as development environments; scratch orgs aren't required.
Production deploys still follow the normal Apex test rules.
questions.source: Salesforce Help: DevOps Center

questions.q: Before a release, a developer wants to check that the changes deploy cleanly to the UAT sandbox, including running local tests, without changing UAT. The team lead says the command below is the wrong tool for a sandbox. Which command should the developer use?
questions.code: sf project deploy validate --source-dir force-app --target-org uat
options: sf project deploy start --source-dir force-app --target-org uat --test-level RunLocalTests --ignore-conflicts
sf project deploy quick --source-dir force-app --target-org uat
sf project deploy preview --source-dir force-app --target-org uat
sf project deploy start --source-dir force-app --target-org uat --dry-run --test-level RunLocalTests
questions.explain: To test-drive a deploy to a sandbox, use a dry run. `deploy validate` is meant for production, so the CLI reference recommends `deploy start --dry-run` with a test level. It validates and runs the tests but saves nothing.
wrong: Without --dry-run, this really deploys and changes UAT.
quick deploys an earlier validation by job ID; it doesn't validate source.
preview only lists what would deploy and possible conflicts; it runs no tests.
questions.source: Salesforce CLI Command Reference: project deploy validate

questions.q: A validation against production succeeded on Monday morning. On Saturday the release manager runs the command below, and it reports that no validated deployment was found. Nothing else has been validated since Monday. What should they do?
questions.code: sf project deploy quick --use-most-recent --target-org prod
options: Validate again, because a validated job ID expires after 3 days
Pass the job ID with --job-id. It stays valid for 10 days, but --use-most-recent only looks back 3 days
Add --test-level RunLocalTests so quick deploy can run the tests again
Run sf project deploy resume --use-most-recent, which turns the most recent validation into a deployment
questions.explain: The job ID lasts longer than the shortcut that finds it. `--use-most-recent` only looks back 3 days. The job ID itself is valid for 10 days from the start of validation, so pass it with `--job-id`.
wrong: The job ID is valid for 10 days; only --use-most-recent is limited to 3.
Quick deploy skips tests because they already ran during validation.
resume watches an operation that is still running; it doesn't deploy a validation.
questions.source: Salesforce CLI Command Reference: project deploy quick

questions.q: The custom field Account.Legacy_Code__c is referenced by the Apex class AccountMapper. The team wants one deployment that updates AccountMapper to remove the reference and also deletes the field. In which manifest should the field be listed?
questions.code:
<!-- package.xml -->
<Package xmlns="http://soap.sforce.com/2006/04/metadata">
  <types>
    <members>AccountMapper</members>
    <name>ApexClass</name>
  </types>
  <version>62.0</version>
</Package>

<!-- deletion manifest: which file? -->
<Package xmlns="http://soap.sforce.com/2006/04/metadata">
  <types>
    <members>Account.Legacy_Code__c</members>
    <name>CustomField</name>
  </types>
</Package>
options: destructiveChangesPre.xml, so the field is deleted before the class is compiled
package.xml, with a delete flag on the members element
destructiveChangesPost.xml, so the field is deleted after AccountMapper is updated
destructiveChanges.xml with <members>*</members> to remove every unused field
questions.explain: Remove the reference first, then delete the field. `destructiveChangesPost.xml` deletes after the other components deploy, so AccountMapper drops its reference first. Post-destructive changes are still processed before tests run.
wrong: Deleting first fails, because the current AccountMapper still uses the field.
package.xml has no delete option; deletions go in a destructive changes manifest.
Wildcards aren't allowed there, and plain destructiveChanges.xml deletes before additions.
questions.source: Metadata API Developer Guide: Deleting Components from an Organization

questions.q: A team is writing CI rules for sf project deploy start. Which two statements about test levels are correct? (Choose 2)
options: RunAllTestsInOrg skips tests that come from installed managed packages
NoTestRun applies only to development environments such as sandboxes, Developer Edition and trial orgs
With RunSpecifiedTests, the deployment passes as long as org-wide coverage stays at 75%, whatever each class reaches
RunLocalTests runs every test in the org except tests from installed managed and unlocked packages
sf project deploy validate defaults to NoTestRun unless --test-level is set
questions.explain: Each test level has a clear scope. NoTestRun is only for development environments, and RunLocalTests skips tests from installed managed and unlocked packages. RunSpecifiedTests needs 75% per class and trigger, and deploy validate defaults to RunLocalTests.
wrong: RunAllTestsInOrg includes managed package tests.
RunSpecifiedTests needs 75% coverage for each class and trigger deployed.
deploy validate requires tests and defaults to RunLocalTests.
questions.source: Salesforce CLI Command Reference: project deploy start; project deploy validate

questions.q: QuoteService gets a Notifier through its constructor. A test must prove that submit() calls Notifier.send exactly once with the quote's Id, without sending anything. What should the test do?
options: Call Test.createStub, then use Test.verify(stub, 'send', 1) after submit() to check the calls the stub received
Stub Notifier with Test.createStub; in handleMethodCall, record each method name and args, then assert
Call Test.setMock(Notifier.class, new NotifierMock()) and read Limits.getCallouts() afterwards to count sends
Subclass Notifier in the test class, redeclare send() as static, and check a static counter after submit()
questions.explain: A stub can count its own calls, because every call passes through it. `handleMethodCall` gets the method name and `listOfArgs`, so record them and assert. The Stub API has no built-in verify.
wrong: There is no Test.verify; the provider must record the calls itself.
Test.setMock is only for callout mocks, and send() makes no callout to count.
An instance method can't be redeclared as static, and statics can't be stubbed anyway.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Build a Mocking Framework with the Stub API; StubProvider Interface

questions.q: A developer wrote a StubProvider for TaxService but can't make InvoiceBuilder use it in a test. What change makes the stub usable?
options: Make TaxService.calculate static, so that Test.createStub can replace it for the whole transaction
Annotate TaxService with @TestVisible, so Test.createStub swaps every new TaxService() in tests
Call Test.setMock(TaxService.class, stub) first, so new TaxService() returns the stub instead
Have InvoiceBuilder accept a TaxService in its constructor, defaulting to new TaxService()
questions.explain: The Stub API makes a stub object; it doesn't intercept `new`. The class under test needs a seam, such as constructor injection, so the test can pass the stub in.
wrong: Static methods can't be stubbed with the Stub API.
@TestVisible only exposes private members to tests; it doesn't redirect new.
Test.setMock only works for callout mocks, not for Apex classes.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Build a Mocking Framework with the Stub API

questions.q: With Debug Mode on, a developer logs this.order (an @api object) from an LWC. Chrome's console shows a Proxy instead of the order's fields. How can they see the real values without changing how the component behaves?
options: Turn off Lightning Web Security in Session Settings, because LWS wraps every @api object in its own Proxy
Remove @api from order while debugging, because the engine wraps only public properties in proxies
Turn on Enable custom formatters in the DevTools Console settings to see the values inside LWC proxies
Turn off secure and persistent browser caching, so the console receives the unwrapped objects instead
questions.explain: A DevTools setting can unwrap LWC proxies for you. Turn on Enable custom formatters in the Console settings. The LWC formatter shows the real values and leaves the proxies in place; with LWS on, it adds extra messages too.
wrong: The proxies come from the LWC engine, not LWS, and turning off security changes behavior.
Changing the decorator changes the component, and tracked objects are proxied too.
Browser caching affects which code loads, not how objects show in the console.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Debug Using Chrome DevTools

questions.q: In a sandbox, a developer deploys LWC fixes several times a day. After each deploy, reloading the record page often runs the old JavaScript until they empty the browser cache. What does Salesforce recommend?
options: Enable Debug Mode for every user in the sandbox, because debug mode turns off all caching of component code
Add a version query string to the component's import statements, so that each deploy produces a brand-new module URL
Set cacheable=false on the component's Apex methods, because cacheable responses keep the old component code
Clear Enable secure and persistent browser caching in Session Settings while debugging, then turn it back on
questions.explain: Browser caching can keep old component code around. In a sandbox or Developer Edition org, clear Enable secure and persistent browser caching while you debug. It hurts performance badly, so turn it back on after, and keep it on in production.
wrong: Debug Mode serves unminified code; it's not the documented fix for stale cached components.
LWC module imports don't take query strings; the platform serves component code.
Apex caching affects data responses, not the component's JavaScript.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Disable Caching During Development

questions.q: An LWC error is caught by framework code, so the console shows only a generic message and the stack points into framework files. How can the developer find the line in their own code that throws?
options: In the Chrome DevTools Sources panel, turn on pause on exceptions and then reproduce the error
Set the Apex Code and Visualforce log levels to FINEST and read the JavaScript stack in the log
Wrap the LWC in an Aura component, because Aura prints the full JavaScript stack for children
Run the component's Jest tests with --coverage, which records the line where the browser failed
questions.explain: Pausing on exceptions stops the browser at the line that throws. That works even if framework code catches the error later. So you land on the failing line in your own source.
wrong: Debug logs record server-side activity, not browser JavaScript stacks.
Wrapping in Aura doesn't change where the exception is caught.
Jest coverage measures local test runs, not errors in the browser.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Debug Using Chrome DevTools

questions.q: A Jest test for an LWC fails. The developer wants to step through the test and the component's event handler with breakpoints in Chrome DevTools. What should they do?
options: Deploy the component with its __tests__ folder to a sandbox and run it from the Developer Console
Run npm run test:unit:debug (sfdx-lwc-jest --debug), then open chrome://inspect and pick the Jest process
Enable Debug Mode for the user, then open the Lightning page in Chrome so that the Jest test runs in its console
Add console.log calls to the test and run sf apex run test --synchronous to read them in the debug log
questions.explain: Jest has a debug mode that Chrome can attach to. `sfdx-lwc-jest --debug` runs Jest under `node --inspect-brk`, and chrome://inspect lists the process for DevTools. VS Code's Debug Test link does the same.
wrong: Jest tests run locally in Node.js, not in an org.
Debug Mode affects code served by the org; Jest tests never run there.
sf apex run test runs Apex tests, not Jest tests.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Debug Jest Tests for Lightning Web Components
